newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Mobistar sees bright future.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Mobistar sees bright future.

text.p: Belgian-French company Mobistar NV, which operates Belgium's second GSM mobile phone network, said on Thursday it was optimistic about its future despite a large loss in its start up year.

"The first months of the financial year 1997 and current developments in the mobile phone market offer Mobistar favourable prospects," the company said in a statement released at a news conference on 1996 results.
Mobistar said it now had over 120,000 customers, up from 68,000 at the end of 1996, which was three times its forecast. It expected to gain at least 100,000 more by the end of 1997.
Mobistar said it believed the penetration by all operators of the Belgian mobile phone market would rise to more than seven percent by the end of the year.
Belgium's first GSM operator, Proximus, a unit of state phone company Belgacom and AirTouch Communications Inc already has more than 400,000 customers.
Belgium's total potential mobile phone market is estimated to be around 10 million equivalent to the country's population.
Mobistar said it would continue to invest in 1997 to further develop its network and services and had therefore increased its capital on April 13 by two billion Belgian francs to 13 billion francs.

Mobistar said all its main shareholders subscribed to the capital increase. Mobistar is now 57 percent owned by France Telecom. Belgian data communications company Telinfo holds 10 percent and nine other Belgian companies, including various units of the Cobepa group, the balance.
